newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council to look at contribution tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council to look at contribution tax.

text.p: The new Brazilian council which is to decide future coffee policy will be responsible for proposing the size of a contribution tax currently set at zero, said the presidential decree establishing the council.
The council could recommend the continuation of a zero tax but expectations are it will suggest a small contribution per 60-kg bag to be put to a promotional fund, traders said.
"This is a subject for discussion by the council....but I believe the council will agree on a tax of $1, maximum $2 a bag," said Jair Coser, president of leading exporter Unicafe.
The tax would apply to exporters, domestic roasters and the soluble coffee industry and would most likely be collected on a monthly basis, he added.
The contribution quota has existed since 1986, according to the presidential decree, but was nullified following the closure of the Brazilian Coffee Institute in 1990, Coser said.

Any new suggested tax level must be put to the National Monetary Council, Brazil's highest monetary policy body, which means a new contribution quota is unlikely to take effect before 1997, dealers said.
The presidential decree took pride of place in today's official government gazette, occupying the front page. Other key details on the council were:
* the council is to approve the crop plan for the sector, including production and export programs for green, roasted and soluble coffee;
* the council is authorised to carry out agricultural and market surveys as well as crop estimates; * the council is to approve each year a proposed budget for monies in the Funcafe coffee fund;
* the council is to regulate action to maintain balanced supply and demand both internally and for export.;
* representatives on the council will serve a two-year term of office;
* should the council's president be unable to attend a meeting, his place will be taken by the executive secretary of the Industry and Commerce Ministry;
* the council is to meet ordinarily every two months and extraordinarily at the request of the council's president or a petition signed by six of the council's members;
* the council's decisions will be taken according to a simple majority and the president will only vote in the case of an evenly split council.
Moreover it is not yet known when the new council will first meet, said Mauricio Assis, head of primary products at the Industry and Commerce Ministry, who will sit on the council.

Roasters had hoped the first session would take place at an industry conference on November 27 to December 1 but this is not possible as the council's president, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles, is not able to attend the conference, Assis said. -- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
